title: introduce-session-facade-compact-connector-and-idempotent-retry-shim-for-tri-sdks
author: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: SDK users reported subtle mismatch in how session reconnects and client-side retry semantics behaved across Python/TS/Go, leading to duplicated side-effects and brittle consumer code. This PR introduces a lightweight session facade plus a compact connector shim that unifies the restart semantics and provides an idempotent retry shim that works consistently across the three SDKs. Key goals: (1) consistent reconnect semantics across languages, (2) idempotent safe default retries for streaming and unary calls, (3) minimal surface-area change for existing callers, (4) small code and runtime overheads, and (5) clear migration path and observability hooks. What this PR changes: - new package/sessionfacade (Python/TS/Go) that exposes Session.maybe_resume(), Session.fence() and a compact connector that normalizes protocol frames between runtime and SDK; the facade keeps lightweight opaque session IDs and an optional per-call idempotency token. - idempotent-retry-shim implemented in each SDK language: default retry policy is conservative (max 2 retries for non-idempotent unary, 0 automatic for streaming append-only by default) and an explicit IdempotencyPolicy object lets users opt into stronger retries. - connection-level state machine hardened: explicit CONNECTED/PAUSED/RECONNECTING/FAILED states, deterministic backoff windows, and a small in-memory ephemeral KV used to avoid duplicate effects for retried requests. - telemetry hooks: session events emitted to existing SDK tracing channels (sdk.session.resume, sdk.session.retry.window) so infra/observability can reason about cross-language behavior. Backwards compatibility: defaults preserve prior behavior for simple usages; advanced consumers can opt-in to the idempotent shim via SessionConfig.enable_idempotent_retries=true. Migration notes: minor changes for advanced streaming users who previously relied on an implicit automatic reconnect; see the README updates and examples included. Tests & validation: added cross-language integration harness that spins up a minimal local mock endpoint to validate duplicate suppression and reconnect ordering, unit tests for state transitions in all three SDKs, and fuzzed permutations for edge timing. Performance: microbenchmarks show ~0.8-1.5% added latency at p95 for cold reconnects and no regression for steady-state token generation. Rollout plan: feature-flag guarded on server side for 2 weeks, opt-in SDK flag for beta customers, then flip default after monitoring. See linked Linear tasks for rollout and GA checklist.

review_comments: Marco Nguyen: Can we avoid persisting the ephemeral KV across restarts? We should keep it in-memory only and document tradeoffs. (resolved)

Leah O'Connor: Suggest moving the default retry ceiling to 2 for unary but make it configurable; also request clearer names for Session.fence vs Session.commit. (author replied: renamed fence->quiesce and added deprecation shim)
Daniel Kim: CI flake on TS integration initially, reran and passed. Also asked for a test to exercise duplicate suppression on concurrent reconnects — added test in commit 4.
Author (Aisha): Addressed review feedback, split large ctor into builder for readability in Go, and added extra telemetry tags for request_id and idempotency_key.
release_notes: SDK: Introduced session facade and compact connector to normalize reconnect and retry semantics across Python/TS/Go.
SDK: Added idempotent retry shim with conservative defaults and an opt-in stronger policy.
Docs: Migration guide and examples for session-based reconnects.
Telemetry: New session-related tracing events (sdk.session.resume, sdk.session.retry.window).
